title: Collinear altermagnetism for 3D chiral higher-order topological insulators
abstract: Despite significant progress in the study of higher-order topological insulators (HOTIs), the chiral $C_4\mathcal{T}$-protected HOTI has remained elusive in electronic materials, where $C_4\mathcal{T}$ denotes the product of a four-fold rotation and time-reversal symmetry. We show that altermagnetism, a recently discovered form of collinear magnetism, provides a new route to realize this elusive phase. Specifically, we construct a microscopic model that combines a three-dimensional topological insulator with a collinear $d$-wave altermagnet on a Lieb lattice. Through analytical and numerical calculations, we show that the magnetism shifts and gaps the surface Dirac cones to produce the desired chiral hinge channels. Finally, we identify promising material classes to realise our proposal. Our results establish collinear altermagnetism as a route to intrinsic chiral higher-order topology and open a new path toward the discovery of $C_4\mathcal{T}$-protected HOTIs in real materials.
summary: This paper proposes that collinear altermagnetism offers a novel pathway to realize chiral Higher-Order Topological Insulators (HOTIs). By constructing a model combining a 3DTI with an altermagnetic order, the authors demonstrate that the resulting symmetry breaking successfully generates the characteristic gapless chiral hinge states. This establishes altermagnetism as a key mechanism for engineering advanced topological electronic materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is to find a physical mechanism to realize the elusive chiral $C_4T$-protected Higher-Order Topological Insulator (HOTI) in electronic materials.
main_result: The authors show that incorporating collinear altermagnetism into a 3D topological insulator model successfully generates the required symmetry breaking and gapless chiral hinge channels.
method: The research employs analytical and numerical calculations, deriving an effective Hamiltonian by coupling a 3DTI to a collinear $d$-wave altermagnet on a Lieb lattice.
model_or_system: The system combines a 3D Topological Insulator (3DTI) with magnetic atoms exhibiting collinear antiferromagnetic order (altermagnetism). The model is built upon a microscopic Hamiltonian that is analyzed via perturbation theory.
key_observables: Chiral hinge channels, gapped surface Dirac cones, and the symmetry protection ($C_4T$) of the topological state.
important_parameters: The breaking of mirror symmetry ($M_z$) and inversion symmetry ($I$) are crucial for achieving the desired HOTI state.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption of weak coupling between the magnetic and topological subsystems, allowing for the use of perturbation theory to derive an effective Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the symmetry requirements for $C_4T$-HOTIs, compare surface state spectra when symmetry is preserved versus when $M_z$ is broken, and show the predicted gapless chiral hinge states in an infinite prism geometry.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the theoretical challenge (chiral HOTIs) to proposing altermagnetism as the solution, developing a detailed microscopic model, and finally using surface/slab calculations to confirm the predicted topological signatures.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter topology, the use of symmetry-protected phases and the explicit construction of novel magnetic orders (altermagnetism) provides a rich theoretical framework applicable to understanding symmetry-driven quantum phenomena in engineered materials.
